subsystems.name: Sensor array
subsystems.role: picks up electrical activity from muscles and nerves at the skin surface.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplifies tiny signals and removes noise.

subsystems.name: Embedded processor
subsystems.role: runs signal processing and machine-learning models on the band itself.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: keeps the band running for a day or more.

subsystems.name: Wireless link
subsystems.role: sends commands to a computer or headset.

subsystems.name: Mechanical housing
subsystems.role: holds electrodes against the skin with consistent pressure.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode layout
buildSteps.detail: Place electrodes a few millimetres apart to capture signals from forearm muscles and underlying nerves; simulate signal quality.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the flexible circuit
buildSteps.detail: Print conductive traces and electrodes on a flexible substrate that conforms to the wrist.

buildSteps.title: Assemble electronics
buildSteps.detail: Solder the analog front end, processor, radio and power management onto the circuit.

buildSteps.title: Develop signal processing
buildSteps.detail: Write filters to remove motion artifacts and power-line interference; extract features like signal amplitude and frequency.

buildSteps.title: Train machine-learning models
buildSteps.detail: Collect labelled data from users performing gestures; train a classifier to map signals to commands.

buildSteps.title: Optimize for on-device inference
buildSteps.detail: Compress the model to run within the band's power and memory limits.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Fit the band to a user, calibrate baseline signals, and test gesture recognition accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Validate in real use
buildSteps.detail: Test in scenarios like controlling a cursor or virtual-reality interface, measuring latency and false activations.

prerequisites.tech: Neural signal decoding from surface electrodes
prerequisites.why: detecting individual nerve signals non-invasively remains very difficult; most systems rely on muscle signals.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes and limited commercial electromyography bands control simple gestures
pathway.unlocks: hands-free control for augmented reality, virtual reality and accessibility.

pathway.milestone: multi-modal bands combining electromyography with ultrasound or impedance sensing
pathway.unlocks: more reliable decoding of intended movements.

pathway.milestone: non-invasive neural interfaces that read nerve signals directly
